clue.text: Bachelor is eager for dogs

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor
someone who itches to do something is eager for it

explanation.surface: A single man is keen to get some pet dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man wanting pets; the plural noun at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Female dogs are called by this word, so it is a narrower term for canines of one sex.

clue.text: Spurious university in Fens

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside the other's letters

blocks.note: fens are marshy ground, i.e. bogs
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A fake university supposedly sited in the Fens of eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat marshland of East Anglia, near Cambridge, which makes a university there plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious and this word are synonyms, both meaning fake or not genuine.

clue.text: Scots order revision of list in article

indicators.note: a revision reworks material, so the letters of the word that follows are rearranged
being in something means sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: the definite article
letters of list rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to revise a list printed in a newspaper article for Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged list sits between TH and E. The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is the chivalric order of Scotland.

clue.text: Fervour in early stage of competition

blocks.note: first meaning: passion or intensity
second meaning: a preliminary round of a race

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm is high in the opening round of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means passionate intensity and also a qualifying round in athletics or swimming.

clue.text: When English celebrate, Tory seaside gang runs riot

indicators.note: running riot means going wild and out of order, so the letters scatter into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of Conservatives rampages at the seaside during English festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like it could be R, but here 'runs riot' is the whole anagram signal and every fodder letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: 23 April, the feast of England's patron saint, is the day the English celebrate their national identity.

clue.text: Ran through short statute recalled by gumshoe

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter
recalling something calls it back, so the shortened word is taken backwards

blocks.note: a gumshoe is a private investigator, PI
a statute is a decree or law

explanation.surface: A private detective revokes a law and stabs someone, a hardboiled crime plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside here, so the detective piece sits next to the shortened, backward statute. A gumshoe is American slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through with a sword is to pierce them, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: Fresh help wanted for ET's orchestral music

indicators.note: something fresh is newly made, so the letters are remade in a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Steven Spielberg's alien ET needs new help, as if advertising for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after ET stands for 'is', linking the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's 1936 piece for narrator and orchestra introduces children to the instruments of the orchestra.

clue.text: Costly staff in medical speciality for ducks, perhaps

definitions.note: duck is an example of the answer

indicators.note: being in something means going inside its letters

blocks.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
dear means expensive
staff as in personnel, men

explanation.surface: Expensive personnel in an ENT department dealing with waterfowl, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' suggests birds, but in northern and Midlands English 'duck' or 'ducks' is an affectionate form of address, like 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone 'ducks' is a term of affection, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Crack team finally removed clamp

indicators.note: removed at the end means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a crew is a team
a vice is a clamp on a workbench

explanation.surface: An elite team is taken off a clamping job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for the team (a crack team); it is the definition, a noun meaning a narrow opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or fissure, so the noun senses are synonyms.

clue.text: Son and daughter called up making claims

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter
called as in given a name

explanation.surface: A son and a daughter phoned up to make insistent requests.
explanation.walkthrough: SDNAMED is read upwards. 'Called up' suggests a phone call, but 'up' is only the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands and claims are both nouns for things insisted on as rightfully owed.

clue.text: Marvin, eg, mixes sugar with it twice

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word it written two times

explanation.surface: Someone named Marvin is baking, stirring sugar in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank Marvin was lead guitarist of the Shadows, the British band behind Cliff Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank Marvin is a famous player of the electric guitar, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Wee drink full of Eastern delight

indicators.note: a vessel full of something holds it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A small Scotch packed with Oriental pleasure, a Turkish delight perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream can mean something wonderful, a delight, as in 'the car drives like a dream'.

clue.text: Position held by retiring anaesthetist

indicators.note: being held by a word means sitting within its letters
retiring means going back, so the run of letters reads backwards

blocks.note: the run of four letters inside ANAESTH-ETIS-T

explanation.surface: A job held by an anaesthetist who is about to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, so it is a synonym of position in the sense of a place.

clue.text: Leaders of region very active in depot as result of famine

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters
being in something means going inside its letters

blocks.note: a depot can be a bus or railway station
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Regional leaders are busy at a supply depot during a famine.
explanation.definitionFit: Famine is a scarcity of food, and starving to death is its consequence.

clue.text: Expect one meeting with head after escapade

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed second, so the one-and-head pair follows the escapade word

blocks.note: an antic is a playful caper
Roman numeral one
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Someone expects to meet the headteacher after a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: Pate is an old or jocular word for the top of the head; antic, now usually plural, is a single caper.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to foresee or look forward to it, a synonym of expect.

clue.text: Irishman leading church's attempt to raise spirits

blocks.note: Sean is a typical Irish forename
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish man heads a church's effort to lift the congregation's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise spirits' suggests cheering people up; here it means summoning ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering where people try to contact the dead, literally raising spirits.

clue.text: Songs from biblical books

definitions.note: names one of the biblical books

blocks.note: first meaning: songs in a show or set are called ...
second meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Hymns or psalms drawn from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' marks the second meaning as one taken from among the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical pieces are called numbers, and the fourth book of Moses bears the same name.

clue.text: After retreat of police, heartless killer's less reliable

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the police letters are read in reverse
with no heart, a word loses its central letters

blocks.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the police withdraw, a cruel murderer is untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: KILLER loses its middle LL. Dicky is British informal for weak or unreliable, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicky means shaky or not to be depended on, so its comparative means less dependable.

clue.text: Good feeding ruined deacon's figure

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt
feeding something puts food inside it, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: letters of deacon rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Good food has wrecked a churchman's waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like the deacon's body shape; it is a geometric figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a ten-sided plane shape, an example of a geometric figure.

clue.text: Small coin, gold rand, showing legendary beast

blocks.note: a cent is a coin of low value
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
R is the abbreviation for the South African rand

explanation.surface: A coin collection including a gold rand bears the image of a mythical creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a creature of Greek myth, half man and half horse.

clue.text: Ecstasy found in camp, leading to convictions

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one letter sits within the other word

blocks.note: a camp is a set of tents
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs discovered at a campsite result in criminal convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convictions' suggests court sentences; it means firm beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenets are principles firmly held, the same as convictions in the sense of beliefs.

clue.text: First couple of twins make rotten bunk

indicators.note: the first couple means the opening two letters of the next word

blocks.note: the opening two letters
to addle an egg is to make it go bad

explanation.surface: Twins spoil a bunk bed, perhaps by bunking off school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed for twins, but it is bunkum, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is short for bunkum, meaning nonsense, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Won't you let me delight over support for bridge?

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the delight word is read backwards

blocks.note: a plea, 'Can't I?'
to revel is to take delight

explanation.surface: A child pleads to be allowed some fun on the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam anchored at one end, used to carry bridges.

clue.text: Press baron holding the door?

definitions.note: describes what the answer does: a noun phrase defined by its function

blocks.note: to jam is to press or squeeze in
B is the abbreviation for baron

explanation.surface: A newspaper tycoon (a press baron) keeps the door open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press baron' reads as one phrase for a newspaper owner, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side post of a doorway, on which the door hangs.

clue.text: Exchange runs out of drink

indicators.note: out of means missing from, so the runs letter leaves the drink

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
brandy is a spirit

explanation.surface: Swapping drinks once the brandy has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To bandy words is to exchange them, as in an argument.

clue.text: Procedures set up ignoring English insult

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the letters read upward
ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: rules are established procedures
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Rules are drawn up that snub the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a disparaging remark, so it is a synonym of insult.

clue.text: Country to store grain, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to garner is to gather into a granary

explanation.surface: A nation stockpiling its harvest, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the R of garner is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African country, the former Gold Coast.

clue.text: Youth stabs old men after party, presaging disaster

indicators.note: stabbing drives something into another, so one piece goes inside
coming after something means being placed second, so the stabbed group follows the party word

blocks.note: a do is a party
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A young man knifes pensioners after a party, a grim news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old men' reads as one phrase but splits into the abbreviation for old plus men.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom-laden means full of foreboding, so it describes something that presages disaster.

clue.text: North Surrey dancing establishment for infants

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters of the county are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
letters of Surrey rearranged

explanation.surface: A dance school in northern Surrey for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where very young children are looked after or taught.

clue.text: Fashion lines not quite the thing?

blocks.note: to forge is to shape or fashion metal
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: Stylish clothing ranges are not quite the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The thing' here means the real thing; a fake is not quite it.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgery is a counterfeit, an imitation that is not the genuine article.
